findings.description: The loop condition uses len(self._keys_by_country), which is the number of distinct countries. It is not the number of cached entries. The cache therefore only evicts once there are more than max_entries countries, so the number of entries is effectively unbounded. With a few countries and many postal codes, memory grows without limit. The max_entries guarantee is broken. The LRU behaviour that the old lru_cache(maxsize=4096) provided is lost.
findings.title: Eviction bound counts countries, not entries

findings.description: clear() empties both maps, so those stay consistent. Separately, _store overwrites an expired entry for the same key without removing it from the key set. That is harmless because the set is idempotent. The real problem is in invalidate_country: if _keys_by_country holds a key that eviction or clear removed from _entries, `del self._entries[key]` raises KeyError. Eviction does keep the two maps in sync, so this is only a latent risk.
findings.title: clear() leaves hit, miss and eviction counters unchanged and is inconsistent with the index

findings.description: source.replace_country is called first, then calculator.rates_changed. Between the two calls, a concurrent lookup can miss the cache, load from the new table, or hit a stale entry. A stale entry is served until invalidation. Because replace_country is not under the cache lock, a loader running inside the cache lock can read the table while it is being swapped. The docstring claim that a lookup never stores a superseded rate does not hold for this path.
findings.suggestion: Perform the replace and the invalidation under the same lock, for example by having the cache expose an operation that runs the replace while holding its lock.
findings.title: Table replacement and cache invalidation are not atomic

findings.description: The loader runs inside `with self._lock`, so every lookup on any key (including cache hits) blocks while one slow rate-source call runs. If the source is a remote or database-backed one, this serialises all tax calculations and stats calls.
findings.suggestion: Load outside the lock and use a per-country version or generation counter to discard results superseded by an invalidation.
findings.title: Loader runs while holding the global cache lock
